as_written_in_papers.quote: The genetic testing found two missense variants in LCAT gene: c.619G>A, p. (Gly207Ser) and c.682G>A, p. (Asp228Asn).
The references used for analysis were: NM_ NM_005502, NM_000039, NM_000229, NM_005505, NM_000384, NM_174936, NM_000253, NM_001033503 and NM_014495 respectively.

cases.statement: One carrier with a clinical diagnosis of fish-eye disease: index case 2, a 47-year-old man, compound heterozygous with c.619G>A p.(Gly207Ser). His parents each carry one of the two variants (which parent carries c.682G>A is shown only in Figure 2, not in the text); they are not separate rows in the batch.

people.label: Index case 2 (IC2)
people.key_phenotypes: ring opacification of the corneal periphery; low HDL (6-16 mg/dl); hypertriglyceridemia; clinical diagnosis fish-eye disease

quotes.quote: A 47-years-old male, referred from primary health center to genetic department for ocular findings combined with analytical changes, with suspected Fish-eye-disease since the age of 45.
In addition to follow-up at nephrology department, he was observed in ophthalmology, and ring opacification of the corneal periphery was revealed.
Analytically, he evolved with low HDL values (6–16 mg/dl) combined with hypertriglyceridemia (158–263 mg/dl), maintained despite the fibrates therapy and diet restrictions.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Corneal ring opacity and low HDL, which the authors call characteristic of fish-eye disease. Four hypoalphalipoproteinemia genes were sequenced on a panel; no rare variants were found in APOA1 or SCARB1, and the only ABCA1 variant reported belongs to index case 1. LCAT enzyme activity is not reported.

quotes.quote: The second patient with hypoalphalipoproteinemia presented ring opacification of the corneal periphery since childhood, characteristic of Fish Eye Disease (Hegele et al., 2020).
Four genes associated to hypoalphalipoproteinemia phenotype were analyzed (ABCA1, APOA1, LCAT and SCARB1).
No rare variants were identified in APOA1 or SCARB1 genes.

segregation.statement: Both parents are heterozygous carriers (one variant each) with low HDL, the father most clearly (29 mg/dl); the sister carries neither variant and has normal HDL (74 mg/dl). No other affected relatives are described.

quotes.quote: The co-segregation study was carried out on the parents, and it was observed that the index patient inherited a different variant from each parent; the sister did not carry any of the mutated alleles (Figure 2).
It is described that heterozygous have HDL-cholesterol levels about half of reference values (Hegele et al., 2020), and in fact the IC parents have low HDL values, most clearly the father (29 mg/dl).
As expected, the non-carrier sister has a normal HDL value (74 mg/dl).

in_trans.statement: In trans with c.619G>A p.(Gly207Ser), shown by testing both parents (each carries a different variant). Which parent carries c.682G>A is not stated in the text. Parents are unrelated.

quotes.quote: The co-segregation study was carried out on the parents, and it was observed that the index patient inherited a different variant from each parent; the sister did not carry any of the mutated alleles (Figure 2).
Parents are unrelated and so the compound heterozygosity was expected in this patient.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense (c.682G>A, p.(Asp228Asn)). The paper's general mechanism statement: biallelic LCAT variants reduce LCAT secretion or function.

quotes.quote: Biallelic variants in the LCAT gene decrease LCAT secretion or function resulting in LCAT deficiency.

authors_classification.statement: The authors classify both variants as VUS under the ACMG guidelines and state they were not described previously.

quotes.quote: These variants are not described previously and are classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS) according to the ACMG guidelines.

concerns: The paper contradicts itself on onset of the eye finding: 'suspected Fish-eye-disease since the age of 45' versus 'ring opacification of the corneal periphery since childhood'.
LCAT enzyme activity and cholesterol esterification were not reported; the fish-eye disease diagnosis rests on clinical and lipid findings.
The patient has a non-functioning right kidney after abdominal trauma, which the authors relate to the accident rather than to LCAT deficiency.
The other allele, c.619G>A p.(Gly207Ser), also appears in batch paper PMID 41551200 (a different person, LCAT-ID0166, compound heterozygous with candidate G-lcat-013).
Which parent carries c.682G>A is shown only in Figure 2 (not in text). The transcript is given without a version (NM_000229).
notes_for_panel: Single proband with a fish-eye disease phenotype; phase shown by parental testing; unaffected sister is a non-carrier with normal HDL. The authors' own classification is under authors_classification. No functional or in-silico data.
